key_insight: Tuning the flame-spraying O2/C2H2 ratio directly improved Ni–Cr–B–Si coating quality, with higher ratios producing denser, smoother, and better-adhered coatings.
engineering_relevance: Process-gas control is a practical lever for optimizing flame-sprayed self-fluxing coatings for wear- and corrosion-resistant surface engineering.
method: Flame-sprayed Ni–Cr–B–Si self-fluxing coatings onto AISI 321 steel
Measured microstructure, porosity, roughness, microhardness, and adhesion strength
evidence_signal: As O2/C2H2 increased, porosity fell from 1.97 ± 0.13% to 0.90 ± 0.09%, roughness dropped from 4.70 ± 0.09 μm to 2.99 ± 0.11 μm, and adhesion rose from 22.14 ± 4.3 MPa to 35.02 ± 3.9 MPa; peak microhardness was 1051.7 HV at 1.1.
watch_item: The reported trends are based on a limited set of gas ratios, so the optimum may shift with spray distance, powder feed, substrate condition, or post-treatment.
paper_title: EFFECT OF FLAME-SPRAYING TEMPERATURE ON THE PROPERTIES OF Ni–Cr–B–Si-BASED SELF-FLUXING COATINGS
